text:
Silas: Opening this thread for follow-ups from today's all-hands about the org changes and hiring plan. Post quick Qs and we'll answer live.

Maya: TL;DR: strategic shift to more product-aligned squads. No involuntary layoffs. We're targeting a net +4 hires this quarter, shifting ~10 roles internally.

Ravi: Can we get clarity on which teams are expanding? Product infra vs host infra?

Maya: Product Delivery and Customer Reliability are the main expansion areas. Core Runtime keeps headcount for platform stability but will flatten some project roles.

Leah: People Ops note: we'll publish the full mapping of affected roles by Wednesday. Managers will get a list of impacted folks to start 1:1s.

Dana: Any change to approval flow for headcount reqs during the transition? I have an urgent req for a data engineer.

Chris: From Finance/GTN: urgent reqs still go through normal approval but we're fast-tracking priority buckets tied to SLA/customer commitments. Flag urgent hires to @Leah + @Chris.

Silas: Is there a temporary hiring freeze? I heard rumors.

Maya: No company-wide freeze. We are pausing non-critical external hires for internal mobility first, but critical customer-impact roles can be greenlit.

Ravi: How about manager spans? Will managers suddenly get more direct reports?

Leah: We will cap spans during transition. Some managers may temporarily have wider spans, but we'll reassign hiring leads or add IC leads to keep load reasonable.

people-ops-bot: :information_source: Reminder: internal transfer window opens Thursday 9:00AM PT and runs 10 business days. Apply via internal careers portal.

Dana: If someone accepts a new role, what's the notice/transition expectation?

Maya: Standard 2-week notice preferred. For priority transfers we'll do 1-week fast-tracks with manager agreement.

Chris: Curious about contractor conversions. Is there a conversion target?

Leah: Yes, converting up to 5 contractor roles into FTEs this fiscal year where it reduces risk (on-call, SRE, and infra ops). Managers should flag candidates.

Silas: A few leaders asked about promotion cycles and compensation adjustments. Any changes there?

Maya: Promotion cycles will remain on the same cadence. Compensation bands unchanged. Salary reviews will proceed as planned; exceptions handled case-by-case.

Ravi: Will there be any new director-level hires or reassignments?

Maya: No major director hires planned this quarter. A small number of squads will report into different directors to improve product alignment; we'll share org charts next week.

Dana: For folks who don't want to move into a new role, what are options?

Leah: Opt-out available. We'll work on internal re-skilling, alternative placements, or a phased transition. No one will be forced into a role change.

Chris: How should teams update their roadmaps given the reorg?

Silas: Product + Eng leads: align with your PMs and update roadmap priorities by end of month. Ops-critical work gets prioritized. If you need temporary triage help, contact @Maya.

people-ops-bot: :white_check_mark: Poll: "Do you have what you need to have conversations with your reports about the reorg?" (24h)

Silas: Thanks for the questions. We'll close this live Q&A Friday and post a consolidated FAQ and timeline. If you want a private chat, DM @Leah or @Maya.
